nodes.description: Parse the input: a UUID (existing case, GET /api/cases/:id) or a natural-language description (new ad-hoc case, build { type, title, context }). Matches `/case-run <caseId | case-description>`.

Determine the case type — compliance | contract | erp-sync | sales — because Themis dispatches a different sub-agent set per type. This is the branch point the current inline call makes implicitly; the graph makes it an explicit, auditable state.

Invoke Themis as Case Coordinator (cli: `run themis --input {action:'case-coordinate', caseId, type, context}`). Themis dispatches per type: compliance -> Themis + Auditor + ChronosAgent (deadlines); contract -> Themis + Auditor + proposal state check; erp-sync -> Themis + ERP sync status + QualityGate; sales -> Themis + lead state + SalesOutreach.

One or more dispatched sub-agents failed or timed out. The long-horizon failure this chapter exists to catch: a partial agent set must not be reported as a complete case status. Retry the failed agent, or mark its track explicitly unavailable in the report — never silently omit it.
Assemble each dispatched agent's finding: Themis summary, Auditor status, ChronosAgent deadline risk where applicable, plus any track marked unavailable by AGENT_FAILURE.
ChronosAgent flagged a deadline at risk. Surface it as its own state rather than a line in a summary — a missed regulatory deadline is the failure mode multi-deadline coordination exists to prevent.
Determine whether any recommended next action is HIGH risk. The skill's documented rule: a HIGH-risk action raises approval_required, which blocks execution pending a human.

approval_required was raised on a HIGH-risk action. Surface the blocking action clearly and provide the approval call: PATCH /api/cases/:id/approve { action, approvedBy }. No HIGH-risk case action executes without it. Same structural gate as Chapters 1/2/5/6; the runner's DEFAULT_GATED_NODE_IDS covers this node id automatically.
Reachable only through HIC_APPROVAL_GATE. Carry out the approved HIGH-risk case action and record that the approval preceded it.
Emit the unified case status: case ID/type/status/priority, deadline, agents dispatched with their findings, required approvals, and one clear recommended next step.

Case remains open across sessions — the multi-deadline, multi-agent state this chapter exists to hold outside chat memory. A new event (deadline approaching, sub-agent update, customer action) re-enters DISPATCH_AGENTS rather than restarting the case.
Terminal for this run — case deferred or withdrawn. Re-enterable; the case row survives.
